preview_en:
Bulgaria are defending a dominant H2H record when they kick off their UEFA Nations League (UNL) campaign against Luxembourg , with this second successive edition in which these sides have shared a group.

Match News and Current Form

Bulgaria will be out to prove they’re better than their FIFA world ranking of 85th in the world as they embark on a third successive campaign in UNL League C. They were trending in the right direction in the 2024/25 edition when they reached the promotion play-offs, but a pair of 2-1 losses to Ireland squashed their hopes and set them on a path to lose nine of their last 14 matches (W3, D2). The Lions look to correct course having lost just three times in 18 group stage games in the third tier (W7, D8), but the confidence garnered from that will be traded off against winning just one of their last eight home matches (D3, L4).

Luxembourg were holding their own in League C, securing second place finishes in both 2020/21 and 2022/23, but found things much tougher last time around when they finished last having won none of their six group games (D3, L3). The Red Lions got their act together and halted what was a six-game losing streak and five-match scoring drought at the time of their promotion/relegation tie with Malta, whom they beat 5-0 on aggregate to preserve their League C status. Their only away game since saw them beat Albania 1-0, a welcome result considering they were winless in their ten road trips prior to the Malta play-off (D2, L8).

Head-to-Head History

Bulgaria are unbeaten in 17 H2Hs against Luxembourg (W14, D3), having kept eight clean sheets in the last ten meetings.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Bulgaria have scored first and led at half-time in four of their last five matches.

Five of Bulgaria’s last seven home matches saw both teams score.

Just one of Luxembourg’s last seven matches produced over 2.5 goals.

The half-time result was replicated at full-time in ten of Luxembourg’s last 12 away matches.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Georgi Rusev has netted Bulgaria’s opener in three of his four international goalscoring appearances, and did the same with both his goals so far this season for his club side. That may be irrelevant if Luxembourg’s Danel Sinani has his say given that just one of his 14 goalscoring appearances in national colours ended in defeat (W12, D1).

Bulgaria are missing their regular captain Kiril Despodov and Filip Krastev through injury, while Luxembourg’s most notable absentee Christopher Martins is also out injured.

Betting Analysis

Both sides tend to be a little goal shy, and hence leaning towards under 2.5 goals and against both teams scoring seems like it has value.

Author: Peter Stavrinou
